issue.title: Rows with accented descriptions are imported twice from overlapping files
issue.body:
September's statement came from our bank's website and October's from our
accounting tool's export, and the two overlap on 30 September. The overlapping
rows without accents were dropped as duplicates, but CAFÉ DE FLORE and SOCIÉTÉ
GÉNÉRALE COMMISSION are now in the ledger twice. They look identical on screen.
In a hex editor, the É in the bank's file is `C3 89`, while the accounting tool
writes `45 CC 81`: an E followed by a separate accent.

input.title: Normalize Unicode in the dedupe key so NFC and NFD descriptions match
input.body:
File: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

dedupeKey joins the raw description into the key, so "É" written as one code point (C3 89) and as E plus a combining accent (45 CC 81) produce different keys and the overlapping row is counted as new. Normalize the description to one canonical form (NFC) inside dedupeKey before joining, so both encodings yield the same key. Ideally also apply the same normalization to the stored keys built by keysFor, which goes through dedupeKey and so is covered by the same change.
